_about: Hand-written program cards for the site's Program tile (openProgramModal in index.html), keyed by the Launch Library program id, with 'names' as a fallback match. English only here; translate_mission_purpose.py translates every text into the site's languages (mission-purpose-gemini.json, 'programProfiles'). Facts: [label key, value] - the label keys are translated in index.html (PROGRAM_CARD_I18N). Status: active | completed | development. logoImage: the program's own image in Launch Library is a logo or emblem, not a photo - shown beside the card's title. logo: our own transparent version, for a logo that comes on a background.

overview: NASA's Commercial Crew Program pays private companies to fly astronauts to and from the International Space Station. Instead of owning and operating its own spacecraft, as it did with the Space Shuttle, NASA buys the rides as a customer, while the companies design, build and operate the vehicles.

The program was created to end the United States' dependence on Russia for access to the station after the Space Shuttle retired in July 2011. From then until 2020, every American astronaut reached the station aboard a Russian Soyuz.
Each operational flight carries a crew of four for a stay of about six months, and the spacecraft stays docked to the station throughout, ready to serve as a lifeboat.
milestones: NASA funds a second round of commercial crew development as the Space Shuttle makes its final flight.
NASA selects SpaceX and Boeing for the final contracts to carry crews to the station.
Demo-1: Crew Dragon's first, uncrewed flight to the station.
Demo-2 carries Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to the station - the first crewed orbital launch from US soil since 2011.
Crew-1 flies the program's first operational crew rotation.
Boeing's Starliner flies its first crew; its two astronauts return to Earth aboard Crew Dragon in 2025.
5.spacex: SpaceX flies its Crew Dragon spacecraft on Falcon 9 from Florida. Crew Dragon was the first commercial spacecraft to carry astronauts to orbit, and it has flown every operational crew rotation of the program so far. The same spacecraft also flies private missions, such as those of Axiom Space.

overview: Commercial Resupply Services is NASA's contract for delivering cargo to the International Space Station - food, water, spare parts, experiments and equipment - aboard commercially operated uncrewed spacecraft.

The first contracts were signed in December 2008 with SpaceX and Orbital Sciences, today part of Northrop Grumman. A second round, CRS-2, awarded in 2016, added Sierra Nevada Corporation's Dream Chaser spaceplane.

Of the cargo spacecraft flying today, Dragon is the only one that can bring large amounts of cargo back to Earth: research samples and hardware return in its capsule, which splashes down in the ocean.
milestones: NASA signs the first cargo contracts with SpaceX and Orbital Sciences.
Dragon becomes the first commercial spacecraft to berth with the station, and CRS-1 flies the first contracted cargo mission.
The second round of contracts, CRS-2, goes to SpaceX, Orbital ATK and Sierra Nevada Corporation.
CRS-21 debuts the second-generation Cargo Dragon, which docks to the station on its own instead of being captured by the robotic arm.
Falcon 9 begins launching Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, after the Antares rocket it flew on was retired.
11.spacex: SpaceX's Cargo Dragon launches on Falcon 9, docks to the station automatically and stays for about a month before returning to Earth with science samples and hardware. Since January 2024 Falcon 9 has also launched Northrop Grumman's Cygnus cargo spacecraft.

overview: The International Space Station is the largest structure humans have ever put in space - a laboratory about the size of a football field, orbiting some 400 km above Earth and circling the planet roughly every 90 minutes.

It is a joint project of five space agencies: NASA of the United States, Roscosmos of Russia, the European Space Agency, Japan's JAXA and the Canadian Space Agency. Assembly began with the launch of the Russian Zarya module in November 1998, and people have lived aboard continuously since November 2000.

Crews carry out research in biology, medicine, physics and materials science in microgravity, and test the technologies needed for longer journeys to the Moon and Mars. The partners plan to operate the station until 2030.
milestones: The first module, Russia's Zarya, is launched.
Expedition 1 arrives - the start of continuous human presence in space.
The Space Shuttle makes its final flight, after carrying most of the station's American, European and Japanese parts to orbit.
The first crew arrives aboard a commercial spacecraft, SpaceX's Crew Dragon.
NASA selects SpaceX to build the US Deorbit Vehicle, which will bring the station down safely at the end of its life.
17.spacex: SpaceX is today the station's main American link to Earth: Crew Dragon carries astronauts, Cargo Dragon delivers supplies and brings research back, and in 2024 NASA chose SpaceX to build the US Deorbit Vehicle that will steer the station into a remote area of the ocean at the end of its life.

overview: Starlink is SpaceX's satellite internet network - thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit, about 550 km up, that deliver fast, low-latency internet almost anywhere on Earth. It is by far the largest satellite constellation ever built; this site shows a live count of its active satellites.

Because the satellites fly dozens of times closer to Earth than traditional geostationary internet satellites, a signal's round trip is short enough for video calls and online gaming. The satellites also pass data between each other with laser links, so traffic can cross oceans without a ground station below.
Service reaches homes, ships, aircraft and remote sites in well over 100 countries and territories, and a newer generation of satellites connects directly to ordinary mobile phones.
milestones: The first two test satellites, Tintin A and B, are launched.
The first batch of 60 operational satellites is launched on a single Falcon 9.
A public beta service begins in North America.
Launches of the larger, more capable V2 Mini satellites begin.
The first Direct to Cell satellites, which connect to regular mobile phones, are launched.
Starship deploys the first 26 V3 satellites - the larger, next-generation Starlink satellites - on its 14th flight.
25.spacex: Starlink is SpaceX's own program and Falcon 9's busiest customer - most Falcon 9 launches carry Starlink satellites. Starlink's revenue helps fund Starship, which now launches the much larger V3 satellites - it deployed the first of them on its 14th flight in September 2026.

overview: Starship is SpaceX's fully reusable launch system: a Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage, together the largest and most powerful rocket ever flown. Both stages are built to return and fly again, which SpaceX expects to cut the cost of reaching orbit dramatically.

Starship is designed to carry more than 100 tonnes to orbit and to be refuelled in space by other Starships - the key to its planned missions to the Moon and Mars. It is developed and tested at SpaceX's Starbase site in southern Texas, with frequent test flights and rapid design changes.
milestones: The Starhopper prototype makes its first hops at Boca Chica, Texas.
NASA selects Starship as the lander that will return astronauts to the Moon.
The first integrated flight test of Super Heavy and Starship.
The launch tower catches a returning Super Heavy booster with its arms for the first time.

overview: Artemis is NASA's program to return astronauts to the Moon for the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972 - and this time to stay, building a long-term presence near the lunar south pole that prepares for crewed missions to Mars.
Astronauts launch on NASA's Space Launch System rocket in the Orion spacecraft. For the landing itself, NASA buys commercial landers: SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon.

The program is international: the European Space Agency builds Orion's service module, other partner agencies contribute hardware and astronauts, and dozens of countries have signed the Artemis Accords on the peaceful exploration of space.
milestones: A presidential directive sends NASA back to the Moon; the program is soon named Artemis.
NASA selects SpaceX's Starship as the first Human Landing System.
Artemis I: an uncrewed Orion flies around the Moon and returns to Earth.
NASA selects Blue Origin's Blue Moon as a second lunar lander.
15.spacex: SpaceX is building the Starship Human Landing System that is planned to land Artemis astronauts on the Moon. Before each landing, a series of Starship tanker flights refuels the lander in Earth orbit so it can travel to the Moon.

overview: Commercial Lunar Payload Services is NASA's way of sending science to the Moon at lower cost: instead of building landers itself, NASA buys delivery services from commercial companies, which design, launch and land their own robotic landers carrying NASA instruments.

The program deliberately accepts higher risk in exchange for lower cost and more frequent flights. Some early landers failed or tipped over on landing, while others landed successfully and returned science from the lunar surface.
milestones: NASA selects the first group of companies eligible to bid for lunar deliveries.
Intuitive Machines' Odysseus becomes the first American lander on the Moon since 1972.
Firefly's Blue Ghost lands upright and completes its full surface mission.
24.spacex: Falcon 9 launched the first program landers to reach the Moon: Intuitive Machines' IM-1 and IM-2 and Firefly's Blue Ghost Mission 1.

overview: Polaris is a privately funded program of crewed missions led by entrepreneur Jared Isaacman in partnership with SpaceX, aimed at advancing human spaceflight technology. It was announced in 2022 with three planned missions, the last of them intended as the first crewed flight of Starship.
Its first mission, Polaris Dawn, flew a four-person crew on Crew Dragon to the highest Earth orbit reached by humans since the Apollo program, and carried out the first commercial spacewalk.
milestones: The program is announced, with three planned missions.
Polaris Dawn launches, reaching an altitude of about 1,400 km.
Jared Isaacman and Sarah Gillis make the first commercial spacewalk, in SpaceX's new spacesuits.
40.spacex: SpaceX adapted Crew Dragon for the mission and designed the new spacesuits used for the spacewalk. Two SpaceX engineers, Sarah Gillis and Anna Menon, flew on Polaris Dawn, which also tested Starlink laser communications from a crewed spacecraft.

overview: Axiom Space flies private astronaut missions to the International Space Station. Each is commanded by a former NASA astronaut and carries private astronauts or national astronauts from countries that want to fly their citizens to space.
Each crew spends about two weeks aboard the station carrying out research and outreach. Axiom is also developing its own commercial space station, intended to take over from the ISS.
milestones: Ax-1: the first all-private crew to visit the International Space Station.
Ax-2 carries the first Saudi woman to fly to space.
Ax-3 flies an all-European crew, including Turkey's first astronaut.
Ax-4 carries astronauts from India, Poland and Hungary - the first from their countries to fly in more than 40 years.
32.spacex: Every Axiom mission flies on SpaceX's Crew Dragon, launched by Falcon 9 from Florida, and SpaceX trains the crews to fly the spacecraft.

overview: The Global Positioning System is the American satellite navigation network behind the location services on phones, cars, aircraft and ships worldwide. Satellites in six orbital planes about 20,200 km up broadcast precise time signals, and a receiver works out its position from the signals of at least four of them.

The system is operated by the US Space Force and is free for anyone to use. The newest satellites, GPS III, are more accurate and harder to jam, and add a civil signal that works together with Europe's Galileo.
milestones: The first GPS satellite is launched.
The system reaches full operational capability.
The deliberate degradation of civilian accuracy is switched off, making GPS precise for everyone.
The first GPS III satellite is launched, on a Falcon 9.
29.spacex: Falcon 9 launched the first GPS III satellite in 2018 and has launched several more since. The Space Force has also moved some GPS satellites to Falcon 9 to keep the constellation on schedule.

overview: The Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites are the American weather satellites that watch the Americas continuously from geostationary orbit, 35,786 km above the equator. Their images feed weather forecasts, hurricane tracking and severe-storm warnings.

The current GOES-R series scans the full disk of the Earth every 10 minutes and the continental United States every 5, and carries a lightning mapper that detects lightning across the hemisphere continuously.
milestones: GOES-1, the first satellite in the series, is launched.
GOES-R, the first satellite of the current generation, is launched.
GOES-U, the last of the GOES-R series, launches on a Falcon Heavy.
The new satellite takes over as GOES-East, watching the eastern United States and the Atlantic.
37.spacex: GOES-U launched on a Falcon Heavy from Florida in June 2024; both of the rocket's side boosters flew back and landed at Cape Canaveral.

overview: NASA's Large Strategic Science Missions - its flagships - are the agency's largest and most capable science missions, each costing billions of dollars: observatories and planetary explorers such as the Hubble Space Telescope, Cassini, the James Webb Space Telescope and Europa Clipper.
They are chosen according to the decadal surveys, the reviews in which each scientific community sets its priorities for the following ten years.
milestones: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched.
Cassini launches toward Saturn.
The James Webb Space Telescope is launched.
Europa Clipper launches on a Falcon Heavy toward Jupiter's moon Europa.
36.spacex: Falcon Heavy launched Europa Clipper in October 2024 - the largest spacecraft NASA has built for a planetary mission - and NASA has selected Falcon Heavy to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

overview: Discovery is NASA's line of focused, lower-cost planetary science missions. Each is proposed and led by a principal investigator and their science team, within a capped budget.
Discovery missions include Mars Pathfinder, the Kepler space telescope, the Dawn asteroid mission, the InSight Mars lander, Lucy and Psyche.
milestones: Mars Pathfinder, one of the program's first missions, is launched.
The Kepler space telescope launches to search for Earth-size planets around other stars.
Lucy launches toward Jupiter's Trojan asteroids.
Psyche launches on a Falcon Heavy toward a metal-rich asteroid.
33.spacex: Falcon Heavy launched Psyche in October 2023 - the first NASA science mission to fly on Falcon Heavy.

names: Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration
overview: Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration, or SIMPLEx, is NASA's program for very small, low-cost planetary science spacecraft. They fly as secondary payloads, sharing a launch with a larger mission to keep costs down.
milestones: Lunar Trailblazer launches alongside the IM-2 lunar lander to map water on the Moon; contact with it is lost the day after launch.
39.spacex: Lunar Trailblazer rode to space as a secondary payload on the Falcon 9 that launched Intuitive Machines' IM-2 lander in February 2025.

overview: Iridium operates a network of 66 active satellites in low Earth orbit that provides voice and data coverage everywhere on Earth, including the oceans and the poles - places no other satellite phone network fully covers.

The satellites are linked to each other, so a call can be passed from satellite to satellite across the sky and down to its destination. The service is used by ships, aircraft, expeditions and emergency services.
milestones: Launches of the original constellation begin.
The first Iridium NEXT satellites launch on a Falcon 9.
The eighth and last Iridium NEXT launch completes the replacement of the entire constellation.
28.spacex: SpaceX launched the whole Iridium NEXT constellation - 75 satellites on eight Falcon 9 launches between 2017 and 2019. The first of them, in January 2017, was Falcon 9's return to flight after a launch pad accident in 2016.

overview: OneWeb is a satellite internet network in low Earth orbit, about 1,200 km up, serving businesses, governments, airlines and ships rather than individual homes.

Its first satellites launched in 2019. The company went bankrupt in 2020, was rescued by the British government and India's Bharti group, and in 2023 merged with the French satellite operator Eutelsat.
milestones: The first six satellites are launched.
OneWeb enters bankruptcy and is bought by the UK government and Bharti.
After Russia stops launching its satellites, OneWeb moves its launches to SpaceX and India's space agency.
The first-generation constellation is completed, and OneWeb merges with Eutelsat.
26.spacex: After Soyuz launches ended in 2022, Falcon 9 launched several batches of OneWeb satellites, helping the company complete its first-generation constellation.

overview: Amazon Leo, formerly Project Kuiper, is Amazon's satellite internet constellation in low Earth orbit, planned at more than 3,200 satellites to compete with Starlink.
Amazon bought launches from several rocket companies - United Launch Alliance, Arianespace, Blue Origin and SpaceX - to deploy the constellation quickly.
milestones: Amazon announces Project Kuiper.
Two prototype satellites are launched and tested in orbit.
Launches of the first production satellites begin.
The network is renamed Amazon Leo.
27.spacex: Amazon bought three Falcon 9 launches for the constellation in 2023, even though it is a direct competitor to Starlink; all three flew in 2025.

overview: Galileo is Europe's global satellite navigation system - an independent, civilian-controlled alternative to the American GPS, built by the European Union and the European Space Agency.
It works alongside GPS in most modern phones, and adds services of its own, such as the search-and-rescue feature that confirms to a person in distress that their emergency signal has been received.
milestones: The first two operational satellites are launched.
Galileo begins its initial services.
Two pairs of Galileo satellites launch on Falcon 9 from Florida.
30.spacex: With Soyuz no longer available and Ariane 6 delayed, the EU launched two pairs of Galileo satellites on Falcon 9 in 2024 - the first time European navigation satellites were launched from the United States.

overview: Copernicus is the European Union's Earth observation program. Its Sentinel satellites monitor land, oceans, ice and the atmosphere, and the data is free for anyone to use.
It is used to track climate change, sea level, pollution, crops and forests, and to map disaster areas after floods, fires and earthquakes.
milestones: Sentinel-1A, the first Copernicus satellite, is launched.
Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich launches on a Falcon 9 to measure sea level.
22.spacex: Falcon 9 launched the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich ocean-monitoring satellite from California in 2020, a joint mission with NASA and NOAA.
